lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience should appear before education.
items.because: Leading with degrees delays the evidence of professional capability.

items.says: The experience section is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Crestline appears before the more recent Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: Coastal Marine Services should be separated or compressed as additional experience.
items.because: Its prominent position makes the résumé open as a diesel-mechanic résumé rather than establish a product or operations direction.

items.says: The product project should sit immediately after the relevant product experience.
items.because: Separating it from Harbor Payments weakens the product-work narrative.

items.says: The dry-dock threshold has no comparison showing an improvement or target achieved.
items.because: A reader cannot judge how meaningful the five-day result was.

items.says: The bullet uses past tense for a current role.
The hydraulic-maintenance bullet describes tasks but gives no result.
items.because: It does not show the effect on vessel operations or inspection readiness.

items.says: The bullet uses past tense for ongoing responsibilities.
The scorecard bullet frames duties instead of showing the action and outcome of the reviews.
items.because: “Owned” and the meeting phrase do not show what the candidate did or what the reviews changed.

items.says: “Retraining 45 pickers on the new layout” is longer than necessary.
The first use of S&OP is unexplained.
“Consecutive” adds unnecessary duration detail.
The strongest result is buried after too many methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the saving of 1,800 driver hours.

items.says: “Which saved” has an ambiguous cause.
items.because: It is unclear whether the saving came from the tool, procedures, training or negotiations.

items.says: The checkout-test result should lead the internship entry.
items.because: The conversion increase is the clearest product outcome in the entry.

items.says: “The three-step flow” is slightly repetitive.
items.because: It slows the A/B-test result.

items.says: RICE Reach is defined incorrectly as support tickets closed.
items.because: Reach estimates affected users, customers or sessions during a defined period, not expected tickets closed.

items.says: The RICE bullet gives no resulting roadmap decision or measurable effect.
items.because: It shows a framework was used without showing what was selected or achieved.

items.says: The Reach input has no resulting estimate or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale behind the prioritization.

items.says: The chargeback analysis gives no financial estimate for the loss by segment.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the magnitude supporting the recommendation.

items.says: The roadmap decision is buried after a crowded chain of methods and does not name the priority.
items.because: Four gerunds precede the result, and the selected problem is unclear.

items.says: A session-randomized test is reported as an effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: Repeated sessions from one customer can occur, so the test directly estimates a session-level effect.

items.says: The five-point lift does not identify its comparison.
items.because: Without treatment and control rates, the reader cannot interpret how it was calculated.

items.says: The bullet repeats the checkout test and five-point lift already reported in line 17.
items.because: It uses a bullet without adding a distinct accomplishment.

items.says: The onboarding bullet does not show the recommendation or decision framing that led to funding.
items.because: The funding looks like a leadership decision rather than evidence that the candidate’s recommendation secured support.

items.says: The launch bullet does not identify the candidate’s specific product contribution.
items.because: It shows the app’s reach and result without showing what the Product Lead personally owned.

items.says: “To 3,100 students with two dining halls” makes the relationship between users and dining halls unclear.
A rise from 400 to 1,150 is not a 150% increase.
items.because: The increase of 750 divided by 400 is 187.5%.

items.says: The wording makes it sound as though the reminders were chosen rather than informed by user research.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase from a 75% baseline is 26.7%.

items.says: The volunteer-system intervention does not show the candidate’s specific role.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what scheduling, coordination or operating work the candidate personally performed.

items.says: The savings estimate does not show the analysis or comparison supporting it.
items.because: A consulting reader cannot judge how the model produced the $2.4M estimate.

items.says: The intake-form improvement has no before-and-after measure.
items.because: The reader cannot judge how much burden was removed.

items.says: Passive wording hides ownership of the intake-form improvement.
items.because: It makes the candidate’s process-improvement role less visible.

items.says: “Final” adds no useful information.
items.because: A recommendation presented for approval is already the deliverable.

items.says: The scheduling-pilot approval repeats the pilot outcome in the quantified savings bullet.
items.because: The second approval statement adds little new evidence.
